taxonomic_note: Current Kew treatment recognizes var. ashei and var. ovata. This learner entry remains at species rank; no variety is assigned without separate evidence.
look_here_first: On adult foliage, inspect the tiny scale leaves for a darker raised, nearly circular to hemispheric resin gland. Then confirm with dark-blue glaucous seed cones and thin shredding bark.
project_tracker_diagnostic: Evergreen shrub/tree with appressed scale leaves bearing raised rounded dorsal glands, finely toothed margins, shredding bark, and dark purplish-blue glaucous seed cones usually about 6–9 mm.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Explicit target-zone records documented in UT North Hays flora, Travis County Balcones Canyonlands plant records, and USGS Honey Creek/Comal County work. No county presence inferred.

morphology_keys.habit: Evergreen dioecious shrub to small tree, often irregular to rounded and sometimes multistemmed.
morphology_keys.bark: Brown to gray bark exfoliating in thin fibrous or shredding strips.
morphology_keys.leaves: Adult leaves are tiny appressed scales; typical blades about 1 mm long with finely toothed margins and a darker raised circular resin gland. Vigorous whip shoots may carry longer awl-like leaves.
morphology_keys.reproductive: Pollen cones are small and terminal. Mature seed cones are berrylike, dark purplish-blue and glaucous, typically 6–9 mm and commonly one-seeded.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Eastern redcedar has a pit-like/depressed adult scale-leaf gland and smaller 4.5–5 mm glaucous cones commonly with 1–2(–3) seeds; Ashe juniper has a raised rounded/hemispheric gland and larger 6.5–9.6 mm glaucous cones usually one-seeded. Kew currently keeps var. ovata within J. ashei, so seed count alone is not absolute. Redberry juniper develops copper to reddish mature cones.

ecological_notes.habitat: Limestone glades, rocky slopes and bluffs, shallow calcareous soils, and oak-juniper woodland of the Edwards Plateau.
ecological_notes.learning_note: A useful genus anchor because the best separation characters are tiny structures on the scale leaves plus cone characters, not tree shape alone.
